answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed traveling market inspector who wanders a fixed circuit of real coastal markets, stamping each day's catch ledger at the reef-side fish market where a beacon flashes the opening price. Inspectors are checked in person at unannounced markets, so one operator cannot staff two circuits on the same day. The license fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real inspector, another full market circuit, and twice the prior fee.
